$comment: The published identity of koru-lambda-core. This file is the single source
for every vector the substrate guarantees; src/vectors.rs mirrors it and a
test asserts the mirror. Language-neutral on purpose: hex strings and
integers only, so a conforming implementation in any language can certify
Changing any value here changes the published identity of the substrate.
scripts/gates/vectors_frozen.sh refuses that unless frozen_for_major and
the digest in conformance/VECTORS.sha256 are updated to match, which makes
the change three visible edits instead of one silent regeneration.

primordials.$comment: Asserted, not derived. Every other value below descends from these.

operator.$comment: synthesize(a, b) = SHA-256(min(a,b) || max(a,b))[0..16], with a==b returning a before hashing.

$comment: The substrate's only free parameter, and therefore the thing that most
needs pinning: two implementations can satisfy every operator case above
and still disagree on every value a consumer folds.
Each byte takes 8 synthesize steps, one per bit, least-significant first,
folding the accumulator with the primordial that bit selects.

folds.$comment: Pins the sequence fold end to end: the anchor rule, the length folded first, and element order. The anchor is `d` because an anchor must not be a byte tip.
folds.name: fold_hi_anchored_at_d
